sources.title: Admission psychiatric assessment
sources.description: Initial assessment on admission. Patient presenting with significant withdrawal and reduced motivation. MDT plan initiated.

sources.title: Risperidone initiated — 2 mg daily
sources.description: De-identified record: risperidone 2 mg daily was initiated. Behaviour, tolerability and adverse effects were planned for clinical review.

sources.title: Nursing behavioural observation plan
sources.description: Nursing team initiated structured behavioural monitoring. Low activity noted across days 1–3.

sources.title: Risperidone increased — 3 mg daily
sources.description: De-identified titration record: risperidone increased from 2 mg to 3 mg daily following review. Location signals do not establish treatment response or tolerability.

sources.title: Psychiatrist review — Day 4
sources.description: Review of presenting symptoms. Medication adjustment under consideration. Limited environmental engagement noted.

sources.title: Risperidone increased — 4 mg daily
sources.description: De-identified titration record: risperidone increased from 3 mg to 4 mg daily. Increased environmental and activity-room engagement appeared in subsequent days alongside OT behavioural activation; attribution to either intervention is not possible from these data.

sources.title: OT behavioural activation initiated — Day 6
sources.description: Occupational therapist commenced graded behavioural activation programme. Initial individual session attended.

sources.title: Nursing review — increased engagement noted
sources.description: Nursing team noted patient spending more time outside bedroom. Engagement with activity room observed.

sources.title: OT session — activity participation strengthening
sources.description: Patient participated in OT session and showed increased engagement with structured activities.

sources.title: First structured group attendance — Day 10
sources.description: Patient attended structured group for the first time. Participation observed as passive but present.

sources.title: MDT nursing update — Day 11
sources.description: MDT noted improved general activation. Peer interaction remains limited. Social participation flagged for review.

sources.title: Psychiatrist review — Day 12
sources.description: Positive trajectory in activation noted. Social engagement remains an area of clinical attention.

sources.title: OT review — engagement consolidating
sources.description: OT session confirmed sustained participation in structured activities. Graded social exposure discussed.

sources.title: MDT ward round — Day 14
sources.description: Full MDT review. Overall activation trajectory positive. Peer interaction domain identified as focus for next phase.

sources.title: Psychiatric admission assessment — Presenting concern
sources.description: Patient described reduced drive, spending most of the day alone, and difficulty initiating usual activities.

sources.title: Psychiatric admission assessment — History and context
sources.description: Family reported a gradual reduction in usual activity before admission. Initial ward observations recorded limited time outside the assigned cubicle.

sources.title: Psychiatric admission assessment — Mental state examination
sources.description: Engaged briefly with interview and gave short responses. Affect appeared constricted. No behavioural disturbance was observed during the assessment.

sources.title: Psychiatric admission assessment — Risk assessment
sources.description: Denied current intent to harm self or others during this review. Risk remains subject to ongoing multidisciplinary assessment.

sources.title: Psychiatric admission assessment — Clinical impression
sources.description: Reduced initiation and social withdrawal require longitudinal observation. Admission assessment alone does not establish the cause of the behavioural pattern.

sources.title: Psychiatric admission assessment — Plan
sources.description: Continue nursing observations, establish baseline ward participation, review medication and invite OT functional assessment.

sources.title: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — subjective
sources.description: Patient agreed to prepare a simple snack and stated, “I can try if the steps are written down.” Reported making sandwiches occasionally before admission.

sources.title: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — objective
sources.description: Attended the 45-minute kitchen session. Gathered bread, egg, mayonnaise and utensils from a written checklist. Required one verbal prompt to sequence egg peeling and mixing. Prepared and plated one sandwich, cleaned the work area with two prompts, and remained in the session throughout.

sources.title: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — assessment
sources.description: Demonstrated initiation with structure and completed a familiar multistep task. Performance supports emerging task participation; one session does not establish independent meal-management ability.

sources.title: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — plan
sources.description: Repeat a familiar cold-meal task with fewer prompts and review carry-over to the ward breakfast routine.

sources.title: Family meeting with sister — Attendees and purpose
sources.description: Patient, sister and Medical Social Worker met to clarify family support, visit preferences and practical discharge needs.

sources.title: Family meeting with sister — Family perspective
sources.description: Sister reported that the patient previously joined family meals but had withdrawn during the month before admission. She identified transport availability for post-discharge appointments.

sources.title: Family meeting with sister — Patient perspective
sources.description: Patient said short visits felt manageable but longer conversations were tiring. He agreed to one further brief visit.

sources.title: Family meeting with sister — Session observation
sources.description: Patient attended 30 minutes of the planned session and answered direct questions. Family contact appears available; preference for time-limited interaction should not be interpreted as unwillingness to engage.

sources.title: Family meeting with sister — Agreed actions
sources.description: Arrange a 30-minute follow-up visit, provide the ward contact pathway, and bring practical support needs to MDT review.

input.guardrails:
# Psych-MAP clinical answer guardrails

These instructions are injected into every patient-level CodeBuddy request. They are safeguards, not clinical policy.

- Answer the clinician's question directly before adding supplementary context.
- Supplementary information must be supported by evidence for the selected patient and selected date range.
- Never manufacture a blind spot merely because it appears in the profession policy.
- Never repeat a topic already covered by the clinician's question or direct answer.
- Surface no more than two concise supplementary pointers to avoid overload.
- Use only supplied evidence IDs; do not infer missing facts, causation, diagnosis, risk level, or treatment effect.
- Keep deterministic retrieval and calculations separate from CodeBuddy synthesis. Do not change verified calculations.
- A supplementary pointer may suggest a topic for review, but must not prescribe, diagnose, or direct treatment.
- Log whether a pointer was surfaced, dismissed, or marked helpful so administrators can review the policy.
- Never promote a newly discovered question cluster into profession policy automatically. Administrator approval is required.

## Doctor questions and evidence requirements

Interpret these topics semantically, including paraphrases; these are not keyword routes or canned patient answers. Retrieve relevant clinical_event facts, including original clinical-document sections, before deciding coverage. Use only the selected patient's supplied records.

- How has the patient been sleeping? Sleep observations or patient sleep reports are needed. Overnight room presence is only a proxy.
- Has the patient been eating? Meal-intake observations or patient reports are needed. Dining-area presence or food preparation does not prove food consumption.
- Has the patient been taking medication? Medication administration or explicit documented taking/refusal is needed. A prescription/change is not administration.
- Has the patient's mood improved? Compare dated mood assessments or patient reports; activity alone is insufficient.
- Has the patient's anxiety improved? Compare dated anxiety/distress assessments or reports; spatial patterns alone are insufficient.
- Have psychotic symptoms improved? Compare documented symptom assessments; never infer from quietness or movement.
- Has the patient reported suicidal thoughts? Quote and date explicit relevant reports/assessments. Missing documentation is not a denial. Denial of intent is not denial of thoughts. A historical note is not a current safety assessment.
- Has the patient experienced medication side effects? Use explicit tolerability/side-effect reports; chronology alone does not establish causation or absence.
- How were outings or home leave? Use leave records and return/debrief reports. Absence of RFID detection does not establish leave or its outcome.
- What feedback has family provided after visiting? Use attributed family feedback, not visitor-area presence. Preserve who said what and when.
- What's the discharge plan? Summarise documented plan and outstanding actions; do not invent dates or arrangements.
- Suitable for stepdown care? Summarise documented MDT assessment and relevant function/support evidence. Do not independently decide suitability; request MDT assessment and service criteria if absent.
- Who will take care of the patient after discharge? Require explicit agreed caregiver arrangements. A visit, relative or transport offer is not agreement to provide care.
- Is the patient willing to continue medication after discharge? Require a documented patient preference/discussion. Current prescriptions or inpatient medication-taking do not establish future willingness.

For partial or insufficient synthesis, populate missingInformation with short requests for the specific records needed. Do not put patient facts, treatment advice or unsupported conclusions in this field. Use partial when relevant evidence exists but does not establish the requested conclusion. Use insufficient when it does not answer the question. Do not ask the user to clarify a clear question just because data is missing: retrieve relevant available notes and report the gap. Do not select unrelated spatial facts to make an answer appear complete.

Keep interpretation text free of digits, including day numbers and date ranges. The application already renders exact dates and values from the selected facts. Say "the selected period" or "the admission assessment" in interpretation text. A day number in the question is not necessarily supported by the cited fact. Return the synthesis object directly; never wrap it inside a "contract" property.

evidenceRows.statement: Day 1 at 18:00 · Risperidone initiated — 2 mg daily: De-identified record: risperidone 2 mg daily was initiated. Behaviour, tolerability and adverse effects were planned for clinical review.

evidenceRows.label: Nursing behavioural observation plan
evidenceRows.statement: Day 3 at 14:00 · Nursing behavioural observation plan: Nursing team initiated structured behavioural monitoring. Low activity noted across days 1–3.

evidenceRows.statement: Day 4 at 10:00 · Psychiatrist review — Day 4: Review of presenting symptoms. Medication adjustment under consideration. Limited environmental engagement noted.

evidenceRows.label: Risperidone increased — 4 mg daily
evidenceRows.statement: Day 5 at 09:15 · Risperidone increased — 4 mg daily: De-identified titration record: risperidone increased from 3 mg to 4 mg daily. Increased environmental and activity-room engagement appeared in subsequent days alongside OT behavioural activation; attribution to either intervention is not possible from these data.

evidenceRows.label: OT behavioural activation initiated — Day 6
evidenceRows.statement: Day 6 at 10:00 · OT behavioural activation initiated — Day 6: Occupational therapist commenced graded behavioural activation programme. Initial individual session attended.

evidenceRows.label: Nursing review — increased engagement noted
evidenceRows.statement: Day 8 at 11:50 · Nursing review — increased engagement noted: Nursing team noted patient spending more time outside bedroom. Engagement with activity room observed.

evidenceRows.label: OT session — activity participation strengthening
evidenceRows.statement: Day 9 at 11:05 · OT session — activity participation strengthening: Patient participated in OT session and showed increased engagement with structured activities.

evidenceRows.label: First structured group attendance — Day 10
evidenceRows.statement: Day 10 at 10:00 · First structured group attendance — Day 10: Patient attended structured group for the first time. Participation observed as passive but present.

evidenceRows.label: MDT nursing update — Day 11
evidenceRows.statement: Day 11 at 11:00 · MDT nursing update — Day 11: MDT noted improved general activation. Peer interaction remains limited. Social participation flagged for review.

evidenceRows.label: Psychiatrist review — Day 12
evidenceRows.statement: Day 12 at 11:30 · Psychiatrist review — Day 12: Positive trajectory in activation noted. Social engagement remains an area of clinical attention.

evidenceRows.label: OT review — engagement consolidating
evidenceRows.statement: Day 13 at 11:40 · OT review — engagement consolidating: OT session confirmed sustained participation in structured activities. Graded social exposure discussed.

evidenceRows.label: MDT ward round — Day 14
evidenceRows.statement: Day 14 at 09:00 · MDT ward round — Day 14: Full MDT review. Overall activation trajectory positive. Peer interaction domain identified as focus for next phase.

evidenceRows.label: Psychiatric admission assessment — Presenting concern
evidenceRows.statement: Day 1 at 10:00 · Psychiatric admission assessment — Presenting concern: Patient described reduced drive, spending most of the day alone, and difficulty initiating usual activities.

evidenceRows.label: Psychiatric admission assessment — History and context
evidenceRows.statement: Day 1 at 10:00 · Psychiatric admission assessment — History and context: Family reported a gradual reduction in usual activity before admission. Initial ward observations recorded limited time outside the assigned cubicle.

evidenceRows.label: Psychiatric admission assessment — Mental state examination
evidenceRows.statement: Day 1 at 10:00 · Psychiatric admission assessment — Mental state examination: Engaged briefly with interview and gave short responses. Affect appeared constricted. No behavioural disturbance was observed during the assessment.

evidenceRows.label: Psychiatric admission assessment — Risk assessment
evidenceRows.statement: Day 1 at 10:00 · Psychiatric admission assessment — Risk assessment: Denied current intent to harm self or others during this review. Risk remains subject to ongoing multidisciplinary assessment.

evidenceRows.label: Psychiatric admission assessment — Clinical impression
evidenceRows.statement: Day 1 at 10:00 · Psychiatric admission assessment — Clinical impression: Reduced initiation and social withdrawal require longitudinal observation. Admission assessment alone does not establish the cause of the behavioural pattern.

evidenceRows.label: Psychiatric admission assessment — Plan
evidenceRows.statement: Day 1 at 10:00 · Psychiatric admission assessment — Plan: Continue nursing observations, establish baseline ward participation, review medication and invite OT functional assessment.

evidenceRows.label: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — subjective
evidenceRows.statement: Day 9 at 09:30 · Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — subjective: Patient agreed to prepare a simple snack and stated, “I can try if the steps are written down.” Reported making sandwiches occasionally before admission.

evidenceRows.label: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — objective
evidenceRows.statement: Day 9 at 09:30 · Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — objective: Attended the 45-minute kitchen session. Gathered bread, egg, mayonnaise and utensils from a written checklist. Required one verbal prompt to sequence egg peeling and mixing. Prepared and plated one sandwich, cleaned the work area with two prompts, and remained in the session throughout.

evidenceRows.label: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — assessment
evidenceRows.statement: Day 9 at 09:30 · Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — assessment: Demonstrated initiation with structure and completed a familiar multistep task. Performance supports emerging task participation; one session does not establish independent meal-management ability.

evidenceRows.label: Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — plan
evidenceRows.statement: Day 9 at 09:30 · Meal preparation — egg mayonnaise sandwich — plan: Repeat a familiar cold-meal task with fewer prompts and review carry-over to the ward breakfast routine.

evidenceRows.label: Family meeting with sister — Attendees and purpose
evidenceRows.statement: Day 12 at 15:00 · Family meeting with sister — Attendees and purpose: Patient, sister and Medical Social Worker met to clarify family support, visit preferences and practical discharge needs.

evidenceRows.label: Family meeting with sister — Family perspective
evidenceRows.statement: Day 12 at 15:00 · Family meeting with sister — Family perspective: Sister reported that the patient previously joined family meals but had withdrawn during the month before admission. She identified transport availability for post-discharge appointments.

evidenceRows.label: Family meeting with sister — Patient perspective
evidenceRows.statement: Day 12 at 15:00 · Family meeting with sister — Patient perspective: Patient said short visits felt manageable but longer conversations were tiring. He agreed to one further brief visit.

evidenceRows.label: Family meeting with sister — Session observation
evidenceRows.statement: Day 12 at 15:00 · Family meeting with sister — Session observation: Patient attended 30 minutes of the planned session and answered direct questions. Family contact appears available; preference for time-limited interaction should not be interpreted as unwillingness to engage.

evidenceRows.label: Family meeting with sister — Agreed actions
evidenceRows.statement: Day 12 at 15:00 · Family meeting with sister — Agreed actions: Arrange a 30-minute follow-up visit, provide the ward contact pathway, and bring practical support needs to MDT review.
